summary: Compact target-verify graph capture ignored the attention backend's existing ragged-graph capability flag. Hybrid Triton plus GDN correctly reports the capability as false, but startup still entered capture and could reach Triton extend_attention_fwd. Unsupported compact graph capture is now skipped, preserving the existing eager fallback selected by can_run_graph.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before control on the unguarded base: capture called warmup even though supports_ragged_verify_graph was false. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-3beed6345a9c/failing-before.txt

Six tests and three subtests passed: unsupported compact capture skips before warmup, supported compact and non-compact capture continue, Triton remains non-capable, hybrid capability is the conjunction of both children, and known capable backends remain enabled. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-3beed6345a9c/passing-after.txt

gpu_execution_evidence: The assigned device was identified as AMD Instinct MI350X, GFX Version gfx950, unique ID 0x5e94f9cc641f4027. The regression exercises graph-capture admission control and imports GPU backends but intentionally launches no GPU kernel; it is not a model-serving or CUDA reproduction.
remaining_limitations: The reported Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 model and DSpark draft weights were unavailable.
The assigned gfx950 ROCm 7.2 device does not reproduce the reporter's B300 CUDA 13.2 environment.
No full model, HTTP serving, CUDA-graph capture, semantic-accuracy, or multi-node claim is made.
The fix deliberately falls back to eager target verification for unsupported compact attention backends; it does not add ragged CUDA-graph support to Triton attention.
